recipes.name: Linguine Pasta with Shrimp and Tomatoes
ingredients_raw: salt and black pepper to taste
1 pound peeled and deveined medium shrimp

steps.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the garlic; cook 2 minutes. Add the tomatoes, and wine. Bring to a simmer and cook 30 minutes, stirring frequently. Once the tomatoes have simmered into a sauce, stir in the butter and season with salt and pepper.

Fill a large pot with lightly-salted water; bring to a rolling boil; stir in the linguine and return to a boil. Cook the pasta uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the pasta has cooked through but is still firm to the bite, about 11 minutes. Drain well in a colander set in the sink.

Season the shrimp with the Cajun seasoning, salt, and pepper. Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Stir in the shrimp and cook until pink on the outside and no longer translucent in the center, about 5 minutes. Stir the shrimp into the pasta sauce, then stir the sauce into the linguine to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Linguine Pasta with Shrimp and Tomatoes
raw_recipe.description: A sauce made from fresh tomatoes is the secret ingredient in this delicious shrimp pasta.

review.reviewBody: I authored this recipe but since it was written and 2 years later published I've made a few changes. I add about 1 cup of cream and about 3 tablespoons of fresh chopped basil at the end. This is so good for a quick and easy meal for company or just a quick and easy meal for your family! Update 12/5/09 - This originally called for 12 oz of angel hair pasta but AR changed it to 16 oz of linguine. Not sure why but you may want to change the amount of pasta to only 12oz.
Used cherry tomatoes and added a cup of chicken stock to the sauce simmered for more than 30 min and topped with some toasted pine nuts.

This recipe was delicious. I did make a few changes, and it turned out amazing! Per the author, I used 12 oz .of angel hair. Make sure you take it out of water while it's still al dente because it will continue cooking when you mix it with the sauce. I added half of a chopped yellow onion with the garlic. I used 2 undrained 14oz cans of diced tomatoes (the ones with basil, garlic, and a few other spices in the can, cut garlic down to 2 cloves in the recipe since the canned tomatoes had garlic in them), 2 diced fresh roma tomatoes (about 1 cup, don't forget to peel the skin), and 1/2 cup of canned crushed tomatoes. I also added a tsp of cajun seasoning to the sauce. I simmered this for a little longer, about half an hour more than recipe calls for. I used a tasty chardonnay, which was great to sip on while cooking as well! I also added a 1/2 cup low fat milk at the end, before stirring in the pasta. I wanted a little creaminess, but didn't want the extra fat and calories of the cream. The milk worked great! I forgot the fresh basil, so I added some dried basil. Topped with fresh parmesan a paired with a lovely salad, and it made for an amazing meal. Thanks for the recipe Cindy!

this recipe was delicious. When I followed her ingredients it seemed like it was missing something, so I put my own spin on it. I used red and green peppers, mushrooms 1/2 onion, 1 cup on heavy cream, and a little sugar since it tasted a little bitter. on the shrimp I added garlic powder along with the cajun seasoning. I topped the dish with basil and parmesan cheese. My husband cleaned his plate. Will definitely make again
After the tomatoes have simmered into a sauce, stir in 1 cup cream and 3 tablespoons fresh basil and heat until warm (but not boiling). I only used 12 oz linguine pasta.

I have made this 3 times in the last month. It is wonderful. Before I gave my review I wanted to try it a few different ways. It is well worth the time to make. Here are my changes. When I sauteed the garlic I added some crushed red pepper. Your choice as to how much. I added 1 tsp. - we like the heat. I used one can of diced tomatoes with the juice and added about 1/2 pint of grape tomates. I also use chicken broth in place of the wne. Half way thru cooking I mashed the tomatoes with a potato masher. Also when cooking the sauce I add 1 TBLS tomato paste. At the end I add 2 TBLS sour cream. Be sure to use medium shrimp. That way you get plenty of shrimp with each serving.

Very good! I used 1/2 pasta and 1/2 spiralized yellow squash to cut down on carbs. Added onions just because. Cooked the squash in a bit of olive oil in the same pan I cooked the shrimp, then added it to the pasta al dente. Will definitely have again.
Bar-b-que peppers and onion , grilled shrimp put all over yellow rice, then used the wine, tomato mixture as a sauce. Had company and everything was gone. Enjoyed

This is an amazing recipe! I used a 28 oz can of petite diced tomatoes with the juice; I just had to cook it down slightly more; I also added 1/2 of an onion, chopped with the garlic and a few extra dashes of the cajun seasoning at the end. Served with fresh grated parmesan cheese - this recipe is amazingly yummy!!! Made it for my mother in law's birthday - whole family loved it!

We loved this! The entire family ate every bite on their plates. I did add extra spices to the sauce while cooking, oregano, basil and Italian seasoning. I used alpine touch instead of salt and 1/2 tsp crushed red pepper because I did not have cajun seasoning. I also used spaghetti because I did not have linguini. I also added two large mushrooms and chopped spinach and followed another suggestion to add 1 cup of cream. 

When I make it again, I will keep the extra spices, add a third mushroom and double the shrimp, as we are all shrimp hounds.

A fabulous dish, but it needs more flavor, and to be thicker. Made as is, it is watery. I subbed the dry white wine with hot chicken broth. Add 2 Tbsps. flour to the hot broth and then into the sauce halfway through simmering. Also, do not be afraid to add more cajun seasoning to the shrimp, coat it well before cooking. As other reviewers said, add a few Tbsps. of fresh chopped basil at the end. Yum! Fresh, delicious Italian cuisine :)
Delish! I added one cup of cream and heated before serving. Absolutely scrumptious!
Fantastic! Butter, shrimp, tomatoes and white wine just go together!

Excellent Dish! I did use 1 lb. 8 oz of frozen medium shrimp and a cup of Heavy Cream at the end for a wonderful sauce. The Cajun seasoning was perfect and can't til tomorrow for leftovers. Used quartered fresh tomatoes and it was outstanding.
Fabulous. Adding it as a go- to meal.
I loved it! It tastes great and it's quick and easy to make. The white wine is the added bonus. I'll be making this again and again. I love shrimp recipes
Amazing recipe. I subbed out the white wine for broth from the shells of the shrimp I used. Saved a little extra money and it tasted delicious.

We liked it. It was easy and we used tomatoes we canned. For just the two of us I adjusted it to 4 servings. I did add a sprinkle of the Cajun seasoning to the sauce when I added the butter. I also shredded some parmesan for topping. I will make this again. This would be good served with a salad. I didn't have salad but made crusty bread instead to go with it and that was good also.
